title: What can I learn from Sean's worst property deal?
excerpt: Sean bought a semi-D in Johor Bahru when everyone seemed to be making money there, and was still paying for it a year after handover. He sums up the four mistakes he made.

question.context: About three years before this video, when everyone seemed to be making money in Johor Bahru, Sean booked a semi-D there. A year after vacant possession he was still holding it and paying the instalments, and young viewers were asking him whether to stretch for property beyond their means.
question.text: What went wrong in Sean's worst deal, and how can a buyer avoid the same mistakes?

answer.quote: not all real estate deals you make money
answer.summary: Sean names four mistakes: buying on emotion when the numbers didn't work, overcommitting until instalments took about 94% to 95% of his income, assuming the developer's name didn't matter, and letting the bad deal weigh on him instead of looking for solutions.

reasons.title: Emotion over figures
reasons.body: The design and renderings were beautiful and the market was hot, so he bought although his calculations didn't make sense.

reasons.title: Overcommitting
reasons.body: With instalments taking about 94% to 95% of his income, he was financially crippled for a time. That only works if you can live on very little.

reasons.title: The developer matters
reasons.body: Established developers tend to stand behind their projects and their after-sales service; the one he bought from did not serve him well after the purchase.

reasons.title: Dwelling on it doesn't help
reasons.body: He let the mistake drag on him for a while before realising the only way out is to look for solutions rather than at the problem.

actions: Run the numbers, and walk away if they don't work, however much you like the design.
Keep the instalment well within your income, with room to live.
Check the developer's track record and after-sales service.
Calculate the downside before buying in a hot market.
If a deal goes wrong, focus on solutions, such as selling or renting, rather than the loss.
caveat: Sean shares this to encourage young buyers rather than scare them: he says the worst outcome wasn't as frightening as he feared, and the lessons made him a better investor.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's English captions for this October 2017 video about a semi-D he bought in Johor Bahru. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased.
